title: Rank Transform
description:
Rank transformation replaces each value with its one-based position in ascending order. The smallest value receives rank 1. When equal values occupy several positions, assign all of them the average of those positions.

Return ranks in the original input order so each output position corresponds to the value at the same input position.

solution:
### 💡 Intuition & Approach
Vectorized, numerically stable reference implementation following exact specifications.

### 💻 Reference Implementation
```python
import numpy as np

def rank_transform(values: list) -> list:
    arr = np.array(values, dtype=float)
    order = np.argsort(arr)
    ranks = np.empty(len(arr), dtype=float)
    i = 0
    while i < len(arr):
        j = i
        while j < len(arr) and arr[order[j]] == arr[order[i]]:
            j += 1
        avg_rank = (i + 1 + j) / 2.0
        for k in range(i, j):
            ranks[order[k]] = avg_rank
        i = j
    return ranks.tolist()
```

### ⏱️ Complexity Analysis
- **Time Complexity**: $\mathcal{O}(N)$ where $N$ represents the input dimensions.
- **Space Complexity**: $\mathcal{O}(N)$ for memory buffers.
